speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue, unintentional weight loss, and abnormal physical examination findings. To begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any fever or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient reports a 6-month history of fatigue and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg (11 lb) despite maintaining a good appetite. He denies any recent changes in his diet or physical activity. He takes no medications and does not smoke or use illicit drugs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning, given your age and the 6-month duration of symptoms. Since you maintain a good appetite yet have lost weight, I need to know if you are experiencing night sweats or any new lumps, such as swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpits.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count with differential
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 16,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 11 g/dL (low), Platelets Normal; Chest_X-Ray: Normal readings.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work shows elevated white blood cells and low hemoglobin, which is concerning for a hematologic malignancy, yet your chest X-ray is normal. Given your age and the duration of symptoms, have you noticed any pain in your bones or joints, or have you experienced frequent infections or bleeding gums?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have 5 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, Good appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CBC results showing leukocytosis (WBC 16k) and anemia (Hemoglobin 11) with a normal chest X-ray are highly suggestive of a lymphoid process. Given your age and the 6-month duration, have you noticed any enlarged lymph nodes, splenomegaly (fullness in your left upper abdomen), or easy bruising?

REQUEST TEST: Lactate_Dehydrogenase (LDH)
REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lactate_Dehydrogenase: 245 U/L (elevated); Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Increased lymphocytes with smudge cells; Abdominal_Ultrasound: Diffuse dullness over the left upper quadrant and right upper quadrant (suggestive of hepatosplenomegaly).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The findings of elevated LDH, anemia, leukocytosis with "smudge cells" on the smear, and hepatosplenomegaly are pathognomonic for a specific lymphoproliferative disorder. Do you have any history of autoimmune diseases, or has your spleen been palpable by anyone else previously?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
